symbols.name: screen_egress
symbols.note: Runs secret floor over channels and paths; returns (channel, rule) tuple or None.

claims.text: Run the unconditional secret floor over everything bound for GitHub.
claims.why: The docstring mentions 'bound for GitHub' but the code does not reference GitHub; the comment is a high-level description not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Returns ``(channel, rule)`` for the FIRST hit, or None if clean.
claims.why: The code returns (channel, hit) inside the loops and returns None at the end.

claims.text: The returned rule is a fixed label / path fragment from ``sensitivity`` -- never matched text, so a refusal can be logged and reported without re-leaking the secret it refused (memstore's ``_scan_secret`` posture, same floor, same reason).
claims.why: The code calls secret_floor_rule which is not defined in this chunk; the claim about 'fixed label / path fragment from sensitivity' and 'memstore's _scan_secret posture' cannot be verified.

claims.text: This comment IS the rendering of the bus.
claims.why: The comment refers to the deliberation section as the rendering of the bus, but the bus file is not in this chunk; the claim about the relationship between the comment and the bus is not verifiable.

claims.text: bus.py records "refused" / "unavailable" / "budget_exhausted" / "anomaly" rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between "three vendors agreed" and "one was never asked".
claims.why: This comment references bus.py which is not in this chunk; the behavior of bus.py cannot be verified.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: This comment references the egress lane and its behavior, which is not defined in this chunk; the claim about naming vs counting cannot be verified.

claims.text: The bus file is the record: it is append-only and hash-chained, so a tampered or truncated transcript is detectable and this comment is not.
claims.why: This claim about the bus file's properties (append-only, hash-chained) cannot be verified from this chunk alone.
